## The Ideal City
:::

::: {.prose-left}
Zamość was built from scratch in 1580. Jan Zamoyski, Chancellor and Grand Hetman of the Crown, bought the land and hired Bernardo Morando, an architect from Padua, to lay out a whole city at once — the Renaissance "ideal city", drawn on paper before a single stone went down. The market square measures 100 by 100 metres. The streets run to a grid. The merchant houses carry arcades on the ground floor so you can cross the town in the rain.

The plan survived. No fire, no war and no later rebuilding erased it, which is rare in Poland and the reason UNESCO put the Old Town on the World Heritage List in 1992. What you walk through is still Morando's town, not a reconstruction of it.

The whole Old Town is a 15-minute walk from your door. Go in the evening, when the arcades are lit and the square empties out.
:::
:::
:::

## What to See

::: {.divider-arch}
:::
:::

::: {.sight-list}

::: {.sight-item}
::: {.sight-icon}
{{< icon arch >}}
:::

::: {.sight-body}
### Great Market Square (Rynek Wielki)

[850 m · 11 min walk]{.sight-distance}

Morando's square is a perfect 100 by 100 metres, closed on three sides by arcaded merchant houses in ochre, pink and green. Several of the arcades have tables outside — it is the obvious place for morning coffee.
:::
:::

::: {.sight-item}
::: {.sight-icon}
{{< icon tower >}}
:::

::: {.sight-body}
### Town Hall

[800 m · 10 min walk]{.sight-distance}

The tower and its fan-shaped double staircase close the north side of the square. You can climb the tower for a view over the roofs, and a bugle call is played from it at noon.
:::
:::

::: {.sight-item}
::: {.sight-icon}
{{< icon church >}}
:::

::: {.sight-body}
### Collegiate Cathedral

[1.0 km · 13 min walk]{.sight-distance}

Morando built it for Zamoyski between 1587 and 1598; it became a cathedral in 1992. The founder is buried inside, in the chapel beside the chancel.
:::
:::

::: {.sight-item}
::: {.sight-icon}
{{< icon palace >}}
:::

::: {.sight-body}
### Zamoyski Palace

[1.1 km · 14 min walk]{.sight-distance}

Zamoyski's own residence, set at the west end of Morando's axis and facing the square down a straight line of street. The army took it over in the 1830s and stripped the Baroque front; it holds the courts today, so you see it from the outside.
:::
:::

::: {.sight-item}
::: {.sight-icon}
{{< icon bastion >}}
:::

::: {.sight-body}
### Fortifications & Bastion VII

[1.2 km · 15 min walk]{.sight-distance}

Zamość was a working fortress that held out against the Swedes in 1656 and was only decommissioned in 1866. Bastion VII is the best-restored of the seven — you can walk the ramparts and go down into the casemates.
:::
:::

::: {.sight-item}
::: {.sight-icon}
{{< icon star-david >}}
:::

::: {.sight-body}
### The Synagogue

[650 m · 8 min walk]{.sight-distance}

Built around 1620 and one of the largest Renaissance synagogues left in Poland. Before 1939 Jews were close to half the town's population; the building was restored in 2011 and is open to visitors.
:::
:::

:::
:::
:::

## Suggested Walks
:::

::: {.prose-left}

### The Renaissance circuit (2–3 hours)

Straight down our street and into the Old Town, then round the plan the way Morando drew it. Take it slowly; nothing here is more than a few hundred metres from the next thing.

- **Leave from Orlicz-Dreszera 32** — 10 to 15 minutes on foot to the square
- **Great Market Square** — the arcades and the painted façades of the merchant houses
- **Town Hall** — climb the tower first, while your legs are fresh
- **Arsenal Museum** — Zamoyski's armoury, at the foot of the palace
- **Collegiate Cathedral** — the founder's tomb and the bell tower
- **Old Lublin Gate** — walled up in 1588 and never reopened
- **Bastion VII** — the ramparts, the casemates and the moat line
- **Back along Grodzka** — shops and cafés on the way home

### The evening walk (1 hour)

Worth doing on your first night. The square is floodlit after dark and most of the day visitors have gone by then.

- Cross the square when it is lit and largely empty
- Eat under the arcades — the restaurants there keep tables outside until late
- Look back at the Town Hall tower from the far corner of the square
- Walk home down Grodzka and Partyzantów, about 15 minutes

:::
:::

## Good to Know
:::

::: {.features-grid}

::: {.feature-card}
::: {.feature-icon}
{{< icon walk >}}
:::

### Everything on foot

The Old Town is compact and flat. From our door the synagogue is 650 m, the Town Hall 800 m, Bastion VII 1.2 km — 8 to 15 minutes each. Once the car is parked you can leave it.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
::: {.feature-icon}
{{< icon parking >}}
:::

### Parking

Free at our place, in the yard, under CCTV. Parking inside the Old Town is paid on weekdays and fills up by mid-morning, which is another reason to walk in.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
::: {.feature-icon}
{{< icon fork >}}
:::

### Eating out

Most of the restaurants sit under the arcades on Rynek Wielki and on Staszica. Book a table at weekends in summer. Ask us and we will tell you where we eat ourselves.
:::

::: {.feature-card}
::: {.feature-icon}
{{< icon basket >}}
:::

### Shops & market

A supermarket is a few minutes' walk from the apartments, open late. The town market off Partyzantów runs in the mornings and is the place for fruit, bread and cheese.
:::
